title: Al-Kawthar: abundance
hook: We have given you abundance, so pray and sacrifice (Surah 108)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Al-Kafirun, a boundary drawn without a threat. Your line was to you yours, to me mine. Day one hundred sixty-six.
screen: `AL-KAFIRUN — TO YOU YOURS, TO ME MINE.`

segments.voice: People can be cruel about grief. In Mecca, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ had buried his little sons. And some of his enemies, the commentators say, turned that loss into an insult. They called him abtar: cut off, a tree with no branches, a man whose name would die with him. Imagine hearing that about your children, in the street. The answer came in the shortest surah in the whole Qur'an. Three lines, ten words in Arabic. And it doesn't start with the insult. It starts with a gift.
screen: `A LOSS TURNED INTO AN INSULT.` → `ABTAR — CUT OFF.` → `THE SHORTEST SURAH.`

segments.voice: Surah one hundred eight begins, in Pickthall's translation: Lo! We have given thee Abundance; So pray unto thy Lord, and sacrifice. Kawthar comes from the root k-th-r, much, many, in an intensive form: not just a lot, but overflowing, more than enough. Commentators give it two meanings, and hold both. The first is every good thing given to the Prophet: the revelation, his followers, his name. The second is specific. A hadith in Sahih Muslim says the Prophet dozed off among his companions, then lifted his head smiling. Asked why, he said a surah had just come to him, and recited this one. Then he asked: do you know what al-Kawthar is? It's a river my Lord has promised me in Paradise, with abundant good. The third line turns to the insult: Lo! it is thy insulter, and not thou, who is without posterity. The word is the one they used: abtar. Muslim commentators point to what came after. The Prophet's name is spoken today by well over a billion people, and his family line, through his daughter Fatimah, is honored across the Muslim world, while the men who mocked him are remembered mostly because this surah answered them. And notice what the gift asks for in return. Not a speech, not revenge. So pray, and sacrifice: turn toward your Lord, and give something away. When you're told you have nothing, count what you've actually been given. Given plenty.
screen: `KAWTHAR — OVERFLOWING, MORE THAN ENOUGH.` · `A RIVER PROMISED IN PARADISE.` · `THE INSULTER IS THE ONE CUT OFF.` · `SO PRAY, AND GIVE.` · then, large: `GIVEN PLENTY.`

segments.voice: Count your abundance slowly, on your fingers if you like: first the things that are easy to miss, breath, your hands, water from a tap; then people, one who loves you, one who taught you something; then small good things from this week. When you run out of fingers, keep going. If you pray, you can end with alhamdulillah.
Al-Kawthar. Abundance, overflowing good, and a river promised to the Prophet; the name of the shortest surah. Today's word.
Your line: given plenty. The gift came before any answer to the insult. One hundred sixty-six days now.

howItsDone: Al-Kawthar is often among the first surahs children memorize and is recited in the prayers; the hadith of the river of al-Kawthar is widely taught.

fork.setup: enemies call the Prophet abtar, cut off, after his sons die. what does the surah do first?
options: name what he's been given: abundance
fork.reveal: it opens with a gift, asks for prayer and giving, and only then says the insulter is the one cut off (108:3).

original.note: Arabic: abundance, overflowing good, from k-th-r, much or many.

trapdoor: what you thought: a surah about having a lot.
what it means: a gift of overflowing good, given to a grieving man called cut off, answered with prayer and giving.
what a scholar hears: an intensive form from k-th-r; Muslim 400 names al-Kawthar a river in Paradise; the insulter's word abtar is turned back on him in 108:3.
recall: the last surah: refuge from the whisperer

chat.says: What's Surah al-Kawthar about? Isn't it really short?
options: A gift of overflowing good, answering a cruel insult after his sons died.
A promise that the Prophet would grow rich in Mecca, with plenty of money.
A comfort that his line had truly ended, and he should simply accept it.
chat.meaning: Kawthar means overflowing good, and a river promised in Paradise. It answers those who called the grieving Prophet ﷺ cut off.

Al-Kawthar.meaning: abundance, overflowing good; also a river in Paradise

abtar.meaning: cut off: the insult thrown at the Prophet ﷺ

Fatimah.meaning: daughter of the Prophet ﷺ, through whom his line continues

Sahih Muslim.meaning: one of the most trusted hadith collections

notes: Please confirm the exact Pickthall wording of 108:1–3, including the parenthetical '(and not thou)'. The voice reads it with 'and not thou' spoken as part of the line.
Sahih Muslim 400 cited from memory; confirm.
Occasion: reports differ on which enemy said abtar (al-As ibn Wa'il is often named); the script says 'some of his enemies'.
'Ten words in Arabic' and 'shortest surah': confirm.
'Well over a billion people' is a loose figure for the global Muslim population.

Audit 2026-09-30: the hook said he lost his sons 'each one' in Mecca, but his son Ibrahim was born and died in Medina, years after this surah; now 'had buried his little sons' in Mecca. 'History is the commentary' (the narrator's own verdict) now reads as what Muslim commentators point to; 'Fatima' spelled Fatimah as on day 116.
